ops.title: Daemon has no Env field, so an Ensure-driven daemon cannot be told where its home is
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the first real-machine E2E.

`Daemon.agent()` (ensure.go:516) renders no `Env` into the plist, and `Daemon` has no `Env` field. A
launchd-spawned daemon therefore inherits launchd's environment, not its launcher's — so if the
launcher resolved a non-default home, the daemon binds a different socket and the two never
rendezvous. The E2E had to route `DAEMONKIT_HOME` through `Daemon.Args` and have the helper
`os.Setenv` it before calling `Serve`.

`deploy` is unaffected: `Config.Agents` is caller-supplied, so a consumer can render whatever `Env` it
needs. The gap is specific to the `Ensure` path, which builds the agent itself.

Whether this is a defect depends on a decision nobody has taken: is `Ensure` meant to work against a
non-default home at all? `paths` resolves through the passwd database precisely so a sandboxed
environment cannot relocate state, which argues the answer is no and the E2E's workaround is the
supported shape. If so, say it in `Daemon`'s godoc; if not, `Daemon` needs an `Env`.

ops.text: A launchd-spawned daemon and its launcher rendezvous on the same socket without routing environment through Args
